interpretation: Every workflow hazard is represented. Seven hazards have registered ML artifacts, but only the listed usable research statuses are eligible for supplementary research output. Drought is invalidated after a target-window defect; three hazards have no defensible supervised model. Zero models are independently validated for operational use.

entries.interpretation: Shared ML contributes extreme-rainfall screening as forcing evidence only. It is not a flood-occurrence, inundation, depth, or impact prediction.
limitations: Rainfall is not a flood observation; drainage, river level, and inundation outcomes are absent.
The weather model is trained at one reanalysis grid point and does not transfer automatically.

entries.interpretation: Shared ML screens 24-hour rapid intensification from best-track history. It does not predict track, landfall, surge, or local wind.
limitations: IBTrACS is a post-event best-track reanalysis, not an operational forecast.
Rapid intensification is rare; held-out event counts are small.

entries.interpretation: Shared ML screens whether a mainshock is followed by a nearby M4+ event. It does not predict earthquakes, mainshock timing, or shaking.
limitations: The USGS catalogue is regionally clipped and capped at 20,000 events.
Aftershock screening does not predict mainshock occurrence or ground shaking.

entries.interpretation: No defensible supervised landslide model is released: the inventory is a reported-event catalogue without a representative non-event sample.
limitations: Reported-event catalogues are biased toward populated areas and accessible roads.
No background/non-event sample exists in the repository.

entries.interpretation: Shared ML screens next-day high temperature at the Kochi reanalysis grid point. It is not an official heatwave declaration or warning.
limitations: Reanalysis grid-point temperature is not a station observation or an official heatwave index.
Humidity, night-time temperature, and local exposure are not modelled.

entries.interpretation: The previous 30-day rainfall-deficit model was invalidated after a target-window construction defect. No usable drought ML output is available until corrected future-only training and validation.
limitations: A 30-day rainfall deficit is a meteorological indicator, not agricultural or hydrological drought.
Soil moisture, evaporative demand, storage, and demand are absent.
Prior drought model metrics are invalidated; corrected target retraining is required.
The previous target builder overlapped most of the supposed future rainfall window with historical features; prior model metrics are invalidated.

entries.interpretation: No defensible supervised model is released: facility-level release labels, controls, and representative non-events are unavailable.
limitations: No quality-controlled release inventory or facility control data are available.
Permits do not establish current emissions or causal source contribution.

entries.interpretation: No defensible supervised model is released: asset condition, network state, and outage/recovery labels are unavailable.
limitations: No verified asset condition, dependency, outage, or restoration dataset is joined.
Mapped roads and facility directories are not an exposure or vulnerability model.

entries.interpretation: Shared ML provides an exploratory concurrent cyclone-proximity/rainfall association. It is not a joint probability, lead-time forecast, or compound impact estimate.
limitations: Cyclone proximity and rainfall are concurrent; the association model has no lead time.
Only 128 cyclone-near days and about 20 compound extreme-rain days are available.
Separate component indicators are not added into a joint probability.

entries.interpretation: Shared ML contributes rainfall screening as forcing evidence only. The deterministic Rational Method flow/capacity comparison remains the decision calculation.
limitations: Drainage capacity and failure state are user-supplied assumptions, not observed.
The Rational Method comparison is a scenario calculation, not a validated flood forecast.
